title: Gujarat-Origin New York Man Pleads Guilty in $9.36M Missouri Gambling Racket
excerpt: Sunilkumar N Patel, 53, admitted running six Missouri arcades as a front for illegal gambling that generated $9.36 million, and now faces up to 20 years in federal prison.
body:
• Sunilkumar N Patel, 53, a New York resident of Gujarati origin, pleaded guilty in federal court in Missouri to charges including conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to operate an illegal gambling business, and money laundering.
  • Patel and his co-conspirators allegedly ran six gambling operations disguised as "internet amusement arcade games" and "skill game arcades" across southwest Missouri, generating $9,362,114 (about Rs 89 crore) in gross proceeds.
  • He was among nine people charged in a 72-count superseding indictment returned by a federal grand jury in Springfield on May 14, 2025, covering operations between July 2022 and May 2025.
  • Patel pleaded guilty before US Chief Magistrate Judge Willie J. Epps Jr. and faces up to 20 years in federal prison on the most serious counts; a sentencing date will be set after a pre-sentence investigation.

An Indian national of Gujarati origin living in New York has pleaded guilty to his role in a multi-million-dollar illegal gambling conspiracy that operated through six businesses in southwest Missouri, federal prosecutors said.

Sunilkumar N Patel, 53, pleaded guilty in federal court in Missouri to charges including conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to operate an illegal gambling business, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and money laundering, according to the US Attorney's Office for the Western District of Missouri.

"and faces up to 20 years in federal prison on the most serious counts; a sentencing date will be set after a pre-sentence investigation."

Six arcades, one cover story

Patel admitted that he and his co-conspirators collectively obtained about $9,362,114 through the wire fraud scheme and illegal gambling businesses, and later carried out financial transactions to launder the proceeds. The operation ran under the guise of "internet amusement arcade games, skill game arcades, and adult arcades." Prosecutors said the businesses instead operated contests of chance, gambling devices and slot machines in violation of Missouri and federal laws.

The six locations included four businesses in Springfield — Big Win Arcade #1, Big Win Arcade #2, Spin Hitters and Vegas Arcade — plus Spin Zone in Joplin and Vegas City Arcade in Branson West. Patel and his co-conspirators also hired local employees to work at the businesses, according to the US Attorney's Office.

One of nine charged

Patel was among nine people charged in a 72-count superseding indictment returned by a federal grand jury in Springfield, Missouri, on May 14, 2025. The indictment alleged that the group operated the businesses between July 1, 2022, and May 13, 2025. All nine defendants were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to operate an illegal gambling business and operating illegal gambling businesses; all nine faced at least one count of wire fraud, while eight were charged with money laundering.

What's next: sentencing

Patel faces up to 20 years in federal prison for conspiracy to commit wire fraud, up to 20 years for conspiracy to operate an illegal gambling business, up to five years for conspiracy to commit money laundering, and up to 20 years each for the money laundering and wire fraud-related counts. Federal law sets the maximum sentences, while the court will determine the actual sentence based on federal sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors. A sentencing date will be set after a pre-sentence investigation by the US Probation Office.

Several federal, state and local agencies investigated the case, including the FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, IRS-Criminal Investigations and police departments in Springfield and Joplin. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant US Attorney Casey Clark.
